stem: A 7-month-old infant has a first episode of wheeze during a coryzal illness; what is the most appropriate bronchodilator approach?

options.text: Start a salbutamol trial because any wheeze at any age should be bronchodilator-responsive
Avoid a salbutamol trial because it is recommended only if the child is older than 1 year
Give prednisolone for 5 days as first-line treatment
Arrange spirometry before deciding on treatment
Send a nasopharyngeal aspirate to guide management

explanation: Salbutamol trial is not recommended in this 7-month-old infant. The appropriate approach is to avoid a bronchodilator trial because the child is younger than 1 year, and provide supportive care with clinical monitoring.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because the bronchodilator trial is not recommended for all wheezy children; the age threshold matters here.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because the source advice limits a salbutamol trial to children older than 1 year, so a 7-month-old should not receive one routinely.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because prednisolone is not the first-line treatment for infant viral wheeze in this setting.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because spirometry is not the deciding test in an acute wheezy 7-month-old infant.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a nasopharyngeal aspirate may support a diagnosis but does not determine acute management.
